items.title: Henry "Booker T." Glass Interview, 1972-05-19
items.q: Billy and Dee Dee was rehearsing at my house. That's where they started. Oh yeah? Billy and Dee Dee started right at my house. They practiced every day.

ctx.x: the whole thing. How did Dee used to play with you? I never heard you mention your

username. Who? Dee Dee. Well Dee Dee and Billy, well they know, you didn't know Dee Dee and Billy, but they started with me. Billy and Dee Dee was rehearsing at my house. That's where they started. Oh yeah? Billy and Dee Dee started right at my house. They practiced every day. It was Sunday. Billy and Dee Dee lived at my house. They'd sleep by my house and everything. Billy and Dee Dee. You played with Mr. Bucko Grammer? Bucko Grammer, Dijama, Gagne. I'm about to see to get them bitches. Yeah, I like seeing.…
A little tin flute? Yeah, tin flute. Paul Barnes learned how to play that. How much did those flutes cost then? We used to pay ten cents for them.

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: That was a book. Glass. Henry Glass. It was his band.

ctx.x: Whose band was that? George Lewis's or what? No.

That was a book. Glass. Henry Glass. It was his band. Oh, I see. And then, no, John Cashmere. Cashmere. John Cashmere. He's a pioneer in that place. It was his band. Oh, I don't understand. He's a pioneer in that place. I played for Lewis during the time, uh, he threw the first ball at, uh, boys home, LaFont's home. LaFont's home. He gave me the trippy on. He gave him the outfit, the boys, uh, suit the boys home. He gave him their baseball suits. And I played, uh, played the dance afterwards, you know. Played for…
